limitations: Every member ref is a snapshot-catalog ref (namespace 'snapshot'), not a live-store version: re-pin before submitting.
Membership is a declared pin and states where a record applies; it infers no causal link between members.

The numeric requirements are Fish 1990 observed ranges proposed as a design envelope, not a feasibility certificate.

payload.mission: Engineer toward a flying fish: explore, with typed models and refusals, what a flying-fish-like glider would require. This is a design-studio project on a generic schema; it does not assert that any design is feasible.

open_questions.text: What measured and modelled quantities could connect a molecular prediction to tissue transport in one specified fish system?
How does a linear instability result relate to the nonlinear pattern a reaction-diffusion simulation produces for a fin-like domain?
Which measured lift and drag coefficients apply to a flying-fish-like body? The Park & Choi tables have not been read, so CL_max, CD0 and e are declared priors.
What is the effective flexural rigidity of an excised fin ray under the clamping that matches its in-fin boundary condition? The beam model sweeps an assumed range.
Is there a sourced upper size limit for a gliding fish? Davenport 2003, the paper that argues one, is unread.

requirements.text: Stay at or above the lightest specimen mass in the source envelope.
Stay at or below the heaviest specimen mass in the source envelope.
Stay at or above the lowest reported wing loading.
Stay at or below the highest reported wing loading.
Every coupling between models is reported as composable, assumption-level scenario, or refused; scenario results keep that label.
Do not claim that an organism is feasible, that a source envelope is a universal feasibility region, or that a model coupling is a biological correspondence.

scale_coverage.note: One molecule-to-fin source (Daane 2021, association in zebrafish); no executable model, no parameter link to wing area.
No structure or affinity input for a fin-patterning protein; the one binding test was stopped at its coverage floor.
A two-cell Delta-Notch model is replayed in this project but it is non-dimensional and not tied to a fish; no cell-to-fin coupling exists.
A reaction-diffusion field sweep exists only for abstract kinetics; no fin-tissue model, no SI length or time scale.
An elastic fin-ray beam with an ASSUMED stiffness range runs; no calibrated fin stiffness exists.
Exact-rational constraint solver, point-mass glide simulation and a fin load bridge run; all rest on declared assumptions.
Fish 1990 allometry only (a measured scaling of wing loading with mass); no developmental model.
Darwin 1859, a phylogeny and a fossil source as context; no ecological model.
No source or model is indexed for this scale in the snapshot.
